plan: My private value is $14. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. Bidding below my value risks losing the item when I would have profited, while bidding above risks paying more than the item is worth to me. Since my value is $14, and I want to maximize potential profit, I'll bid exactly $14. This ensures I win if the item is worth more to me than to others, and I'll only pay the second-highest bid.

With a private value of $34, my optimal strategy is to bid close to, but slightly below my true value. This protects my potential profit margin. Since values are drawn randomly and independently, I can't predict others' values. A bid around $33-$34 seems strategic - high enough to likely win if my value is near the top, but not so high that I risk overpaying. I'll aim to capture profit by paying less than my true value.

My private value is $33. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is typically to bid my true value. This means bidding $33 ensures I only win if the item is truly worth more than the second-highest bid. If I win, I'll pay less than my value. If I bid less, I risk losing an item that could generate profit. With no prior round history and values drawn independently, a true-value bid is most rational.
